# 5.4 Actions

`Action { start (clip time), duration, curve, end: Patch }`. To evaluate a
property at clip time *t*: start from the clip's base props, apply the end
patch of every action that finished at or before *t* (in start order),
then if *t* is inside an action, interpolate from that state to the
action's end patch along its curve. Numeric fields interpolate; colors
interpolate in OKLab with straight alpha, known by key — `video.shadow.color`,
`video.chroma.key` (rgb only), `text.color`, `text.outline.color`,
`text.backdrop.color`, `text.word_style.active_color`, `.spoken_color`,
`.upcoming_color` and `text.word_style.active_pill.color`; a key whose ends
are equal stays exact (§11 G-43); booleans and strings switch at the end. Actions
on a clip may not overlap (`add_action` refuses). Video, audio and text
properties all go through the one list with typed patches.

**The timeline's volume line is a view of actions, not keyframes** (§11
AU-80…AU-83). It draws the plan's gain for a clip; a drag on it writes the
clip's `set_audio {volume}` or the end of the action whose `audio.volume`
is in force, and a point added with ⌥ is an action's END: `add_action` from
the latest action end before the press, or — inside an action whose end
names only `audio.volume` — `set_action` shortening it and `add_action` for
the rest, which carries its end volume and its curve (so an eased action's
shape is re-eased on each side). Nothing is stored that actions do not
already store; an agent makes the same point with those ops.

**Every audio setting the tap runs animates too** (§11 AU-85…AU-88): the
pan, the mono fold, the channel pick, the EQ, the hum notch, noise
reduction, the gate, the leveller's target and limits (§11 AU-66), the de-esser, the
compressor, the limiter and isolation's Amount. The plan carries each audio segment's points — the
clip's evaluated audio at the voice's ends, each such action's ends and the
1/30 s grid inside an eased one (§7.2) — and the tap joins them with straight
lines on an absolute sample grid, so the preview and an export agree. The
rule is the one above, with two additions: `isolation` is present at 0, so an
action toward 0.8 ramps from 0; and an EQ slope, the hum's mains and its
harmonics are switches, held until the action's end. Volume, the fades and
ducking were already the envelope's; the duck, `keep_pitch`, the fade
shapes, the voice effect and a nest clip's own keys are not animated. A gate
or limiter keyed on at an end runs for the whole track from then, and an
isolation render is made for a clip whose base Amount is 0 when an end asks
for one.

**A graphic clip's props are a fourth target** (format version 13, §11
G-34), with a door of its own: an end's `graphic: {props, kinds}`. A
`number` ramps and arrives fractional, never rounded; a `color` ramps in
OKLab with straight alpha, as `interpolateColors` blends (§11 G-40;
`#00000000` to `#ffffff` is `#63636380` halfway); a `string`, `boolean`,
`enum` or `asset` switches at the end, and `""` is no image in an end
(§11 G-42); a prop whose schema entry says `animate: false` is refused
(§11 G-41).
A colour is known by the end's `kinds`, never by the value's shape; two
numbers ramp whatever `kinds` holds. The props a patch names are checked
against the op's `schema`; a stored end is never re-checked.

**A media clip's rate is a fifth target** (format version 27, §11 SR-10):
`speed`, a number at the top of an end beside the groups. The rule above on
one number: the rate in force is the clip's `speed`, then each ended
action's `end.speed` in start order; inside the first action spanning *t*,
when it names a speed, `r_from + (r_to − r_from)·ease(u)`; held after. An
action ending at the rate already in force changes nothing. The clip keeps
its slot: the rate changes how much source it reads, `S(t) = ∫₀ᵗ rate`, in
closed form per curve (∫₀ᵘ ease: u²/2, u³/3, u² − u³/3, u³ − u⁴/2), so its
out point is `in + round(S(duration))`, and an action edit that would read
past the media's end is refused (§6). Only a `media` clip ramps; a `speed`
in any other clip's end, or one that is not a number, is inert.

**Lists interpolate per index** when the two sides are the same length and
each pair of entries agrees on the keys that say WHAT the entry is — a
filter's `kind`, a region's `kind` and `shape` — and switch at the end
otherwise; the hold is per entry, so a list in which one region changes
shape still interpolates every region beside it. That is the crate's rule
and not one list's (`actions.rs`), so `video.filters` and `video.obscure`
are both governed by it with no code of their own. The wider set of
discriminants is deliberately confined to list ENTRIES: in a list an
entry's only identity is its index, so a changed `shape` gives no way to
tell a reshaped region from a replaced one, while `video.spotlight` is one
named object whose `shape` is a property of it — an action that moves that
spotlight from a rect to an ellipse still interpolates its geometry, as it
always did.

**A curve's points interpolate per point** (format 17, §11 GR-12): a channel
of `video.curves` is a list of `[x, y]` pairs, so the list rule above lerps
two curves of the same count point by point, and a convex mix of two rising
x sequences still rises. One rule is the curves' own (`actions_curves.rs`):
before the lerp, a channel that is the **identity** on one side (absent
included — the state writes an absent channel as `[[0, 0], [1, 1]]`) and a
curve of a different count on the other is **aligned**: the identity side
takes the other curve's x's with y = x, its first point `[0, 0]` and its last
`[1, 1]`, so a grade animates from neutral, and back to it. Two non-identity
curves of different counts **blend their values** (§11 GR-34): the list rule
holds the list at its start value `a`, so the evaluated props hold `a`, and
the recipe and `clip_state` publish the channel as `{from: a, to: b, t}` for
0 < t < 1 (t the eased progress), which the compositor draws as
`(1 − t)·a(x) + t·b(x)`, exact at both ends. The core samples no spline and
the blend is never in a file: a split mid-blend writes `a` as the head's end,
and the tail blends `a → b` over the rest. An identity curve in an END patch
is kept as written and means "animate to neutral" (a `null` there would remove the key,
the rule below); the inspector's Reset inside an action writes it so. The
evaluated end is clamped like every other value, and an identity channel
evaluates to none.

The hue curves (format 20, §11 GR-32), `hue_hue` and `hue_sat`, follow the
same rules in their own units: two of the same count lerp per point (x
linearly, never across 0°/360°); an identity (every value the neutral, the
state writing an absent one as `[[0, 0], [180, 0]]` or `[[0, 1], [180, 1]]`)
meeting a curve of another count takes that curve's x's with the neutral
value; two non-identity hue curves of different counts blend their values
(§11 GR-34), in degrees or as a gain.

**A qualifier's hue centre takes the short way round** (format 18, §11 GR-13):
two present ranges of `video.qualifier` interpolate per number, but a hue
centre is an angle, and 350 → 10 lerped as numbers would sweep through 180.
Before the lerp (`actions_qualifier.rs`), when both states hold a centre more
than 180° apart, the TARGET's centre moves by ±360 (350 → 370), and the
evaluated end's clamp brings the lerped value back into [0, 360) (`rem_euclid
360`): 350 → 10 passes 355, 0, 5. Two centres exactly 180° apart go linearly.
Only the target of the action the time is inside is touched; an ended
action's end is merged as written. A range turned on or off, and `invert`,

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in

  refusing only for `refusingErrorCodes`, -11833 and -11855) and the codec

  lane: every pass's peaks, loudness, sync and speech decodes run on it, at
  most two at a time, first in first out, on a queue of its own and never on
  the Swift cooperative pool, where synchronous reads would stop every
  `AVAssetReader` in the process (spec §11 #367).

(orig §4, §1g)

**Proposed D6 — every time-varying effect is a pure function of (clip,
frame).** Grain, scanlines and shake use a clip-local frame index and a
seed taken from the clip id. They never read the wall clock or a previous
frame. Echo, trails and true motion blur stay out. R5-5 already made motion
unseeded; a seed arrives only with E4's clock. (orig §4)

**Proposed D7 — nothing moves content out from under an obscure region.** A
stage that moves pixels either carries the region with it, or hides by BOTH
positions.
Carrying the region: flip transforms the quad, not the sampling coordinate;
Hiding by both positions: a fragment is hidden if its own position or its
colour's source position lies in the region. This covers E4's remaps and
mirror.

The review caught the draft breaking this rule twice. (orig §4, §10)

**Overturned by measurement** (orig §5, §10): E8's whole-media cache became
a per-clip WINDOW cache; E9's foreground subject on video was dropped
because it flickers; E9 gained a "no subject" rule, without which a
screencast would be erased.

## The deferred candidates, E3–E9: what each proposed

The original's schema versions (v9–v15) and op counts are stale. The format
### E9 — Remove Background (orig §6 E9, §5b; D5)

`video.cutout` is `{subject: person|foreground, feather}`.

`person` uses `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` at `.balanced`, with a
FRESH request per frame. `.fast` is stateful; `.accurate` runs at 1.7×
realtime and needs 1.7 GiB per minute; `foreground` applies to images and
stills only.

A new `MediaImporter+Masks.swift` computes 10 masks per second of source,
only for the windows that clips show. They are written as 8-bit PNGs under
`cache/masks/<media>-<subject>/`, made from the CODED buffer. The compute
device is pinned in the marker, and proofs compare against the cached masks,
never a recomputation.

**"No subject" rule, per CLIP WINDOW:** if no mask has at least 0.5 % of its
pixels above 127, the clip draws UNCUT.

In the compositor: the core emits `source_t`; Swift binds the nearest mask
as `texture(2)`, sampled through `orientedUV`; the mask multiplies coverage
at step 7; a frame whose mask is pending draws uncut.

# The effects spike — offline voice effects through AVAudioEngine (2026-09-15)

Five programs, run from a shell on macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple M2 Max, whose
output answers the seven questions a "voice effects" design asks before it
leans on `AVAudioEngine`'s offline manual rendering: pitch shift, reverb,
delay, EQ shelves and bands, and `AUDistortion`'s presets rendered per clip
into a cached file. None is a proof; each is an instrument, tracked so the
numbers can be reproduced rather than believed.

All five share `fx_common.swift` — one synchronous renderer (a fresh engine,
manual mode enabled first, the units in series, `renderOffline` in a loop of
4096-frame calls, no `async`, no run loop) and the measurements taken of what
it renders. Scratch output goes to `../work/effects_spike/` (untracked).

| Program | Answers | Build (from this directory) |
|---|---|---|
| `fx_throughput.swift` | q1 × realtime per unit and a 4-unit chain, from a file, a buffer and a source node, with the file write; q6 a 10 s window 30 s in, cold, and whether it equals a slice of a whole render | `xcrun swiftc -O -parse-as-library -target arm64-apple-macos26.0 fx_common.swift fx_throughput.swift -o ../work/effects_spike/fx_throughput` |
| `fx_presets.swift` | q2 the SDK enums, each component's `factoryPresets` and parameter tree, every reverb and distortion preset on speech (level, tail, spectral bands), hand-built telephone/radio/robot/bit-crush; WHEN a preset takes effect | same line, its own name |
| `fx_determinism.swift` | q3 two fresh engines, chunk size 4096/1024/333, file vs buffer vs source node, four renders at once, the cache file's bytes (CAF, WAV, M4A); run it twice and `diff` the outputs for the cross-process half | same line, its own name |
| `fx_alignment.swift` | q4 lag against the dry signal (bursts, clicks, speech), reported latency/tailTime, tails past the input end; q5 TimePitch at ±700…±3000 cents and overlap 3/8/32 | same line, its own name |
| `fx_constraints.swift` | q7 formats (mono per unit, 22.05 kHz, int16, mono and 44.1 kHz render formats), misuse (frames over max, play before start, schedule after play), defaults that silently do nothing, engine reuse, a background thread, `.mov`/AAC sources. Each test runs in its own child process, because AVAudioEngine reports some misuse by an Objective-C exception Swift cannot catch | same line, its own name |

Run each from this directory (`../work/effects_spike/fx_alignment`, …).
`FX_FIXTURES` and `FX_WORK` override the fixture and scratch directories.

## Fixtures

Made into `../work/effects_spike/fx/` (the same sentence the silence spike
used, so the two spikes speak about the same file):

```sh
mkdir -p ../work/effects_spike/fx && cd ../work/effects_spike/fx
say -o speech.aiff "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. [[slnc 1200]] Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs. [[slnc 800]] How vexingly quick daft zebras jump."
F=/opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg
$F -y -v error -i speech.aiff -ar 48000 -ac 2 -c:a pcm_s16le speech48s.wav
$F -y -v error -i speech.aiff -ar 48000 -ac 1 -c:a pcm_s16le speech48m.wav
$F -y -v error -stream_loop -1 -i speech.aiff -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=110:sample_rate=48000:duration=60" \
  -filter_complex "[0]aresample=48000,atrim=duration=60[s];[1]volume=-12dB[t];[s][t]amix=inputs=2:duration=first:normalize=0,pan=stereo|c0=c0|c1=c0" \
  -ac 2 -ar 48000 -t 60 -c:a pcm_s16le long60.wav
$F -y -v error -f lavfi -i "aevalsrc='if(eq(mod(n\,24000)\,12000)\,0.9\,0)':s=48000:d=10:c=stereo" -c:a pcm_s16le clicks.wav
$F -y -v error -f lavfi -i "aevalsrc='if(between(mod(n\,24000)\,12000\,12479)\,0.5*sin(2*PI*1000*n/48000)*(1-cos(2*PI*(mod(n\,24000)-12000)/480))\,0)':s=48000:d=10:c=stereo" -c:a pcm_s16le bursts.wav
```

`speech48s.wav` is 498,689 frames (10.39 s); `long60.wav` 60 s of it looped
over a −30 dBFS 110 Hz tone (no digital silence); `clicks.wav` and
`bursts.wav` put one impulse / one 10 ms Hann-windowed 1 kHz burst at
0.25 s + k × 0.5 s. `fx_constraints` also reads `../media/speech.mov` (PCM),
`../media/AV.mov` and `../media/toneA.m4a` (AAC).

## Host state worth naming

The run of 2026-09-15 was on a machine at a load average of 58–66 on 12
cores (another session's work), so every × realtime figure is a floor under
contention and varied up to 1.6× between runs; the ranges in the design
record are across three runs. The default output device was "MacBook Pro
Speakers" at 48 kHz; a 44.1 kHz render format rendered and reproduced on it,
but no second output device was available to switch to.

# Remove Background — the Vision spike (2026-09-15)

Two programs and a fixture script, run from a shell (under the terminal's TCC
attribution) on macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple M2 Max (ANE 16 cores), asking
whether a cached per-media cutout mask can be built on Vision's
`VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` and `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest`
instead of a shipped model. Instruments, not proofs. Both programs share
`vision_common.swift`: stills drawn into the 32BGRA IOSurface buffer
`AVAssetReader` hands the app, the requests with a compute-device pin
(`auto` / `cpu` / `gpu` / `ane`, and `cpuforce`, which sets the CPU on a
request that does not list it), and the mask copied out as row-packed 8-bit
bytes (a float mask as `round(clamp(v,0,1)·255)`). Everything is synchronous
`VN*` API — no `async`. Scratch output goes to `../work/effects_spike/`.

| Program | Answers | Build (from this directory) |
|---|---|---|
| `vision_stills.swift` | `shape` q1 (revisions, devices, output class/format/size per quality and pixel format, the foreground's four outputs, mask size against five input sizes); `cold` / `warm` q2 per request, quality, device and size (Vision work timed alone, copy-out excluded); `det` / `cmp` q3 (fresh vs fresh, reused vs fresh — person segmentation is a `VNStatefulRequest` — and, run twice, against the previous process's dump); `content` q4/q5 (observations, instances, coverage; `MASK_PNG_DIR` writes the masks); `cache` q6 per-mask bytes | `xcrun swiftc -O -parse-as-library -target arm64-apple-macos26.0 vision_common.swift vision_stills.swift -o ../work/effects_spike/bin/vision_stills` |
| `vision_job.swift` | `job` q2 the realistic job: `AVAssetReader` decode, one mask per 0.1 s of source (or every frame), modes `decode` (floor) / `fresh` / `reused` / `sequence` (`VNSequenceRequestHandler`), optional dump of every mask; `cmpdump` q3 two dumps mask by mask; `stats` q7 consecutive-mask MAD and coverage; `cachesize` q6 a whole job in raw / PNG / LZFSE at native, 256-long-edge and 256×144 | `xcrun swiftc -O -parse-as-library -target arm64-apple-macos26.0 vision_common.swift vision_job.swift -o ../work/effects_spike/bin/vision_job` |
| `vision_fixtures.sh` | every still and video below | `sh vision_fixtures.sh` |

Typical calls (from `../work/effects_spike/`):

```sh
bin/vision_stills shape vision/frames/person_desk.png
bin/vision_stills warm vision/frames/person_desk_4k.png person-balanced 30 ane
bin/vision_stills det vision/frames/person_duo.png person-fast auto det   # run twice
MASK_PNG_DIR=masks bin/vision_stills content vision/frames/*.png
bin/vision_job job vision/video/job_screen_60s.mov person-balanced auto fresh 10 dumps/a.bin
bin/vision_job cmpdump dumps/a.bin dumps/b.bin 512 384
bin/vision_job stats dumps/sduo-fg-mask-fresh.bin 512 512
bin/vision_job cachesize dumps/a.bin 512 384 1920 1080
```

Kinds: `person-fast`, `person-balanced`, `person-accurate`, `fg-observe`
(the instance-label buffer), `fg-mask` (`generateMask(forInstances:)`, native
512×512 float), `fg-scaled` (`generateScaledMaskForImage`, image size float).

content.content:
generic families map onto the set: `serif` → Source Serif 4, `sans-serif`
  → Source Sans 3, `monospace` → IBM Plex Mono (named on the engine's
  `fontdb::Database`). `cursive` and `fantasy` are not mapped and are warned
  like any family the set lacks. The engine's font selector queries the
  text's OWN families only; usvg's default selector, which appends `serif`
  as a last fallback, is not used, because with `serif` mapped every
  missing family would then draw in Source Serif 4 with no warning, and
  "no fallback" above would be false. A family that is exactly `serif`,
  `sans-serif`, `cursive`, `fantasy` or `monospace` (case-sensitive, as usvg
  matches the keywords) is a CSS keyword and is written UNQUOTED by the
  standard library and `measureText`'s probe — quoted, it would name a
  family called "serif", which the set lacks; every other family is quoted
  as above. The standard library's default family stays Montserrat, and a
  `<text>` with no `font-family` still falls to usvg's default "Times New
  Roman" and is still warned.
- **G-7 — A graphic draws at its own size, and crosses the FFI as
  premultiplied BGRA** (road map 10 §4, 2026-09-25). A graphic has a
  `width` and `height` in canvas pixels — the module's `meta.width/height`
  if it declares them, else the canvas size at the time of the add — and,
  like a nest's, the size is frozen: a later canvas change does not re-lay
  out a graphic. It rasterizes at exactly that size, 1 source px = 1 canvas
  px, as a shape does; scale, position and rotation are the layer's. The
  engine writes premultiplied BGRA8 in sRGB into a buffer the app owns,
  the format `LayerRenderers` already uploads, so tiny-skia's RGBA is
  swizzled once, in Rust, and nowhere else. The maximum side is 8192, the
  renderer's own cap.
- **G-8 — A failing graphic shows its error in preview, answers it to the
  agent, and stops an export** (road map 10 §4, 2026-09-25). In PREVIEW a
  module that does not compile, or a frame that throws or times out, draws
  an ERROR CARD in the layer's box — a dark red fill, a 2 pt red border and
  the first diagnostic in IBM Plex Mono with its line and column — and never
  the last good frame, which would hide the error from a person scrubbing.
  `render_frame` and `render_graphic` return the diagnostics as text beside
  the image. An EXPORT compiles every module a clip in the range names
  before it starts and refuses on a compile error, listing each; a frame
  that fails during the export aborts it, naming the graphic and the frame.
  An error card is never written into a video. Built by G3c (road map 10
  §10.6): the card's border is 2 PIXELS of the layer's texture, and the
  missing module draws a card of its own; `render_graphic` was built by
  G4b (road map 10 §10.7): a failing frame is its cell's error card, through
  the same painter.
- **G-9 — A graphic has its own timeline: `in` and `length`, and `split`
  pins it** (road map 10 §4, 2026-09-25; built by G2b). `graphic.in`
  (ticks, ≥ 0) is where on the graphic's own timeline the clip's first
  frame falls; `graphic.length` (ticks, or `null`) is how long that
  timeline is, and `null` means "it ends with the clip", which is what a
  fresh clip wants: stretch the clip and the animation stretches its outro
  to the new end. `split` gives the right half `in + cut` and pins BOTH
  halves' `length` to the original's effective length, so the animation
  continues across the cut and plays its outro once, at the true end.
  `trim_start` advances `in` and `trim_end` never changes `length`, so
  trimming a graphic cuts it as trimming media cuts a file. There is no
  source bound: a clip longer than `length` keeps calling `render` with
  frames past `durationInFrames`, and what it draws there is the module's
  business. The core computes the frame: `frame = floor((in + clip time) /
  frame_ticks)` on the canvas grid and `ctx.durationInFrames =

content.content:
preview. A module in the project's `graphics/` is listed under This
  Project whatever its `category`.
- `schema` is optional (`{}` when absent). It declares the props (below).
- The module is the only source of code: no `import`, no `eval`, no
  `Function`. The standard library below is already global.
- `frame` is an integer counted from the clip's first frame.

## `ctx`

| key | what |
|---|---|
| `fps` | the project's frame rate, e.g. `30` or `29.97002997` |
| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
| `durationInFrames` | the clip's length in frames |
| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, clamped to 0–1 |
| `width`, `height` | the graphic's size in pixels |
| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas |

Write every coordinate in terms of `ctx.width` and `ctx.height` (or a unit
such as `const u = ctx.height / 1080`) so the graphic draws at any size.

## The schema

At most 64 keys. A key is letters, digits and `_`, starts with a letter or
`_`, and is at most 32 characters. Every entry needs a `type` and a
`default` of that type; `label` (else the key) and `help` (a tooltip) are
optional. Any entry may say `animate: false` (a boolean; absent is `true`):
an action never animates that prop, and the inspector writes it to the clip
even while an action is selected — for a count, a layout mode or a data
series a ramp would break.

content.content:
- `FrameWriter.swift` — a `CGImage` and a format in, a URL out, no panel:
  Save Frame and `render_frame` both call `writeFrame`, so their PNGs are
  byte-identical by construction; `writeFrame` labels a rendered frame BT.709
  (`frameSpace`, §11 PR-11; `labelled` does the same for an APNG's frames;
  an HLG project's frame is `hlgSpace`, BT.2100 HLG, and JPEG is refused for
  it, HD-13), `pickable` relabels an HLG frame so a pick reads its raw
  values, and `write` is for snapshots, sheets and tiles. PNG keeps a NIL properties
  dictionary (anything added changes the file); JPEG flattens onto BLACK at
  0.9; HEIC is `UTType.heic`, never `public.heif`.

**Captions.** A caption is an ordinary text clip, which is what makes burn-in
free.
- `CaptionLayout.swift` — placement ONLY (snap, abut, drop sub-frame
  cues, a new front-most track), shared by every producer, and
  `CaptionCues` at its foot — the FIVE cue rules (≤ 2 lines, ≤ 42
  characters, ≤ 6 s, a frame between cues, and never two speakers in
  one cue), used only by a producer that must INVENT line breaks. An
  SRT brings its own. `Word.speaker` defaults to nil, so every caller
  that knows nothing about speakers is byte-identical to what it was.
  `place` takes a `CaptionStyle` and the run's `CaptionLooks` (`looks:`,
  `.none` by default, handed to `pagePatch`; spec §11 W-15): `.subtitles` is the
  Caption-preset
  path, byte for byte for a cue with no speaker (a speaker's cue adds its
  palette `color`, spec §11 R6-22); a word style writes
  `CaptionStyle.pagePatch` per page — the pager's own props at the page's size (a shrunk one or the
  style's), its wrap `width`, and the cue's `words` in CLIP time — at the
  style's `y`. `replacing` removes caption tracks WITH
  their clips as the plan's FIRST ops (a removal mints no id, so the
  new track is still `next_id`), and `replaceableTracks` is the one
  test of which qualify: named "Captions"/"Captions N", AT LEAST ONE
  clip, only text clips, each overlapping a job's `span` — an empty caption
  track is never replaced. `isCaptionTrackName` is the one caption-track

content.content:
Each cue uses the **Caption** text preset: Source Sans 3 Regular at 3.5% of the canvas height, centred, on a 60% black backdrop, wrapping at 80% of the canvas width, with its box centred 38% of the frame height below the middle.

## Caption styles

The five word caption styles make the large, one-row captions used in shorts and reels. Instead of a cue, each clip holds a **page** of words with each word's timing, and the word being spoken is drawn the way the style says. All five are white with the spoken word marked. They are sized to the shorter side of the canvas, so a vertical and a horizontal canvas get the same text height.

| Style | Typeface | Case | How the spoken word shows | Position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Subtitles** | Source Sans 3 Regular | As written | — (two-line cues, above) | 38% of the frame height below centre |
| **Highlight** | Montserrat Black, black outline | UPPERCASE | Turns yellow and pops to 112% | A quarter of the frame height below centre |
| **Pill** | Montserrat ExtraBold | UPPERCASE | Sits on a violet pill | A quarter of the frame height below centre |
| **Karaoke** | Montserrat ExtraBold | As written | Words turn yellow as they are said and stay yellow; words still to come are dimmed white. Up to two lines | 28% of the frame height below centre |
| **Build** | Anton, black outline | UPPERCASE | Words appear one by one; the newest is yellow and pops to 115% | A quarter of the frame height below centre |
| **One Word** | Bebas Neue, black outline | UPPERCASE | One large word at a time, popping to 120% | 18% of the frame height below centre |

The text is 7.5% of the shorter canvas side, and 12% for One Word. The four display faces ship inside the app under the SIL Open Font License.

### How pages are filled

A page is filled to the width it actually measures in its style on your canvas, not to a word count:

- A page fills up to 86% of the canvas width, on one line (Karaoke: up to two).
- It ends early at a pause of 0.25 s or more, after a word ending in `.` `?` `!` or `…`, after 3 seconds on screen, or at a change of speaker. One Word pages hold one word each.
- A comma, semicolon or colon just before the width runs out moves the break back to it, if the page is already at least half full.
- A single word too wide for the frame shrinks, down to 80% of the style's size, before it wraps.
- A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, or runs up to the next page when the gap is under 0.25 s, so the row does not blink between pages.
- Pages never run past the end of the clip they came from.

### The preview

The preview under the Style row shows a sample page drawn by the same renderer the canvas uses, at this canvas's proportions. It uses the first words of the first clip's cached transcript when there is one, and "This is how it looks" otherwise. A word style shows two frames, with the first word active and then the second. A ticked **Fill words as spoken** shows the fill half done, and a ticked **Slide the pill** shows the pill half-way through its slide. **Dim in pauses** is not previewed.

## Looks for word captions

Three checkboxes under the Style popup each add a look to a word style's pages. Each is off until you tick it, and the sheet remembers each one between runs. A box that does not apply to the chosen style is greyed out and does nothing, but keeps its tick for when you switch back.

| Look | What it does | Works with |
|---|---|---|
| **Slide the pill** | The pill slides from the previous word to the one being said, over 0.2 s (or less when the next word comes sooner), instead of jumping. | Pill |
| **Fill words as spoken** | The word being said fills from left to right as it is spoken, taking at most 0.6 s. The part already said is in the highlight colour; the rest is in the upcoming colour (Karaoke's dimmed white), or not yet drawn in Build. | Highlight, Karaoke, Build |
| **Dim in pauses** | The page fades to half opacity during a pause of 0.25 s or more, then comes back before the next word. It also dims before the first word when that word starts late, and after the last word until the caption ends. Each fade takes 0.1 s. | All five word styles |

With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style selected, a note under the boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." The on-device recogniser stretches each word's time across the silence after it, so few pauses are long enough to dim.

*Agents:* `transcribe`'s `slide`, `fill` and `dim`. Each is false unless given, never what the sheet last chose. `true` is refused by name with a style it would not show on, or with `place: false`; `false` is always accepted. A placed run given any of the three lists the looks that were on under `looks`.

## Restyle a caption track

A style is fixed when the captions are generated. To change it, generate again with **Replace** ticked:

1. Open **File ▸ Generate Captions…** over the same clips.
2. Choose the new word style and looks.
3. Tick **Replace: existing captions**. The line under it names each track it will remove, with its caption count, for example "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)."
4. Press **Generate**.

The old tracks are removed and the new one takes their place at the front, all in one undo step. With AssemblyAI the cached transcript is reused, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed.

**Replace** is live only for a word style, and only when there is a track it may replace. That means a track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. Tracks outside the run's scope are left alone.

## Editing captions

Captions are text clips, so the inspector's Clip tab edits them under **Text**: Content, Font, Style, Outline, Backdrop, Box, Reveal and Presets. Select several captions to change them together.

On a word caption page:

- **Case.** The style's capitals come from **Text ▸ Style ▸ UPPERCASE**. Untick it to show a page as written. Case is applied when the page is drawn, so the Content box shows the words as written, and changing case never drops the word timing.
- **Word style colours.** There is no inspector section for a page's word style (highlight colour, pop scale, pill colour). To change them, generate again with a different style, or have an agent use `set_text`'s `word_style`.
- **Editing the words.** Changing the text while keeping the same number of words keeps every word's timing. Changing the number of words drops the timing, and the page then shows plainly. The Content section notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". The same rule holds whether you edit in the Content box or in place on the canvas (double-click the page).
- **Reveal.** The text reveals (typewriter, word fade, line rise) do not apply to a timed page. The Reveal section says "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply."
- **Trimming and splitting.** These keep each word on the speech it times. Retiming a page by dragging it moves its words with it.

# Samples

Real recordings the owner made for working on Frame Job's handling of real material, as
opposed to the synthetic media `tools/proof/` generates with ffmpeg. A proof, a manual
check or a decision may name one; each row says what the file is and what it measures, so
a change that claims to improve it has a before to compare with.

| File | What it is | Measured |

- **`set_canvas {width?, height?, fps?, background?, rescale_clips?, fit_new_clips?,
  timecode_frames?, output?, blending?}`** — `rescale_clips` multiplies every clip's `x`, `y`, `scale` by the size
  ratio. Changing fps normalizes top-level and every stored nest's clip starts, source-bounded
  durations, action spans, present base motion/text timing and a graphic's `in` and `length`, plus
  top-level markers (§11, D7-3, G-18·b); a ramped clip's speed actions are snapped but not clamped
  into it, and its duration is held again against them (§11 SR-19 (g)). Size-only and same-fps
  edits leave legacy timing alone.
  `output` (`sdr` or `hlg`, format 23, §11 HD-2, HD-13) sets the project's dynamic range and
  changes no clip or grade; the output the canvas has is an identity, and another value is
  invalid input naming serde's list (`unknown variant \`pq\`, expected \`sdr\` or \`hlg\``).
  `blending` (`encoded` or `linear`, format 24, §11 GR-18, HD-16) sets how layers blend and
  changes no clip or grade; the blending the canvas has is an identity, and another value is
  invalid input naming both (`unknown variant \`gamma\`, expected \`encoded\` or \`linear\``).

  where `keep_range` can go wrong. FC1's tests cover each kind, and FC2 proves frames and samples
  against the source.
- **Many documents.** Thirty shorts opened at once would approach the instance's
  forty-document deadlock; FC-82 closes each after queueing.
- **Bet 3's interface.** FC9 needs bet 3's planner as a function applied to a document it did
  not create. If bet 3 lands only as a command that makes its own copy, FC9 makes two documents
  per short until that is fixed.
- **Consolidated media.** A source whose media sits inside its own package gives shorts that
  point into that package; moving it means a relink. Media files are never copied (FC-21).

### Not in this bet

- Any score, virality figure or engagement prediction (FC-67).
- Ranking without an Anthropic key, on-device ranking, or Apple FoundationModels.
- Ranking for an outside agent inside Frame Job (`find_clips` answers the analysis; the agent
  ranks).
- Publishing, scheduling, platform upload, titles or thumbnails for platforms.
- Finding clips across several projects or a footage library, or a `search_media` index.
- B-roll, music, zooms or punch-ins added to a short. Punch in on cuts is the next tier.
- Removing pauses in a short. It is a later option, asked at FC8a.
- Linked vertical versions that follow the source's later edits. That is bet 3's to decide.
- Translated captions, platform safe-zone overlays and named platform export rows (the next
  tier's publish slice).
- Visual signals (faces, gestures, shot changes) as readings. Bet 3's and bet 6's Vision
  analysis may add them later.

input.content:
## Bet 3 — Make Vertical Version with on-device subject tracking

### Goal

A creator finishes a 16:9 edit and chooses **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**. Frame Job opens a
copy of the project at 9:16 (1080 × 1920 from a 1080p canvas, 2160 × 3840 from a 4K one) or 1:1.
In the copy:

- every full-frame picture fills the tall frame and follows the face, the person or the salient
  region that Vision found on the Mac, as eased x, y and scale actions on the clip's own action
  lane, which the creator selects and nudges on the canvas like any other action;
- a shot with nothing to follow (a screen, a landscape, a two-shot too wide to crop) is shown
  whole over a blurred copy of itself;
- a cut inside a clip (an export of another edit, imported as one file) is a hard cut in the
  framing too;
- word captions are paged again for the narrow frame from their own words, so corrections made
  by hand survive, and subtitles take the narrow frame's measure;
- a graphic that filled the 16:9 frame is re-sized to the tall one and lays itself out again;
- every other layer (a camera bubble, a title, a logo) keeps its relative place;
- existing zooms keep what they showed: each is composed with the framing, never left aiming at
  16:9 targets.

The same planner is a command on its own: **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** frames the selected clips on
the canvas they are on (a 4K talking head on a 1080p canvas, a 16:9 clip dropped into a vertical
project). After bet 2, a screen recording's vertical version follows the cursor. After bet 5, a
two-person wide shot follows whoever is speaking. Later, if the owner chooses, one project holds
several **shapes** of one cut (linked versions), so a trim in the 16:9 cut is a trim in the 9:16
one.

Nothing is uploaded, nothing needs a key, and every result is an ordinary undo step and an MCP
tool.

### Owner's answers applied

- **"Add all: 1-6."** Bet 3 is in the road map "creator-jobs", prefix VR.
- **"Remove all explicit non-goals."** Spec §1's "auto-reframe (heavy pixel work or ML, outside the
  compositor's one-pass shape)" is lifted by CJ0. This bet supplies the sentence for it (VR-1).
  Lifting it schedules nothing beyond what is below. Motion blur on pans, stabilisation and
  optical flow stay unscheduled here.
- **"Anything that requires significant AI should require that the user has supplied a key."**
  Nothing in this bet uses a language model or a cloud model. Vision's rectangle and saliency
  requests are on-device Apple frameworks that run today without a key, so under the orchestrator's
  reading they are not "significant AI" and no VR control is ever disabled for a missing key
  (VR-2). If a later phase wanted a model to choose framing by meaning, it would fall under the key
  rule; none does.
- **"The recorder can ask for input monitoring."** Bet 2's. VR5 reads typing bursts from bet 2's
  sidecar when present and works without them.
- **"Cutting one real video per lead segment … alongside the first bet. OK."** The owner's two
  trial videos (a talking head and a screen tutorial) are this bet's end-to-end material (sample
  VR-E). Their vertical versions, watched on a phone, are the bet's trial (JOB-35), recorded as
  VR-38 the way GR-9 recorded grading's. That verdict also answers the linked-versions question
  at VR7.
- **The owner did not choose between a regenerated copy and linked versions.** The recommendation
  (VR-3) is the copy first (VR1–VR4, no format bump), with the planner's output shaped so that
  linked versions (VR7–VR9, a format bump) reuse it unchanged. Linked versions are asked at VR7,
  after the trial.
- **The orchestrator's defaults, each of which the owner can change:** VR phases run in one lane
  in order VR1 → VR2 → VR3 → VR4. VR5 and VR6 may run in another lane once VR2 and their other
  bet's phase have landed. VR7–VR9 run only on the owner's yes at VR7. Decision IDs are VR-n0…n9
  per phase. Bet-level decisions VR-1…VR-9 are recorded at CJ0. Manual checks are numbered
  JOB-30…JOB-39 provisionally. VR7's format bump is provisional until it lands.

### How it fits the tree

Facts at `d0661e5d`. Line counts are `wc -l`.

**Placement and the canvas.**
- Spec §5.3 and `core/src/edit_zoom.rs` (467) :38–55 give the one placement rule (★): `canvas(q)
  = anchor + s·R(θ)·(c + q)`. `video.x` and `video.y` are canvas pixels from the canvas centre,
  `scale` is uniform, and a region is in source pixels from the cropped rect's centre. The module
  doc also solves (★) for a region with rotation and the `SCALE_MAX` clamp. The reframe arithmetic
  is a second solution of the same equation and cites it.
- `core/src/edit_fit.rs` (61) :52 `fill_scale` is `max(cw/sw, ch/sh)` clamped to `SCALE_MAX`. A
  1920 × 1080 picture on a 1080 × 1920 canvas fills at ×1.778, so the tall frame sees a window
  607.5 px wide of the 1920 (31.6 %). On 1:1 it sees 1080 of 1920 (56 %). A 1080p source is
  therefore upscaled ×1.78 in a 1080 × 1920 export, and a 4K source is downscaled ×0.89.
- `core/src/edit_canvas.rs` (251) :71: `set_canvas`'s `rescale_clips` multiplies top-level `x`,
  `y` by their own axis ratio and `scale` by the smaller ratio, and **does not rescale action end
  patches** ("an animated move on a resized canvas therefore keeps its old target"). It never
  touches nested clips (a nest's canvas is frozen: `core/src/model.rs` (570) :392,
  `core/src/edit_nest.rs` (338) :223). Spec §6c :150 says the same.
- `core/src/model_query.rs` (551) :217 `source_size`: a media, still or image clip's size is the
  media record's (the displayed, oriented size); a nest's is its frozen canvas; text has none.

**Actions.**
- Spec §5.4 and `core/src/edit_action.rs` (595, at the cap) :63 `overlapping_action`: no two
  actions on one clip may overlap, of any kind. Volume-line points are actions on the same list
  (AU-80), so an ordinary A/V clip often already carries actions.
- An action's x, y and scale interpolate together with one curve (`Curve`: linear, ease_in,
  ease_out, ease_in_out; `core/src/model.rs` :452). The set of placements that cover a canvas is
  an intersection of half-spaces in (x, y, scale), so it is convex. A lerp of two covering states
  on one curve covers at every frame between them. The coverage guarantee in VR-24 rests on this.
- `core/src/speed_map.rs` (414) :295 `source_at(t)`: clip time to source time through speed,
  ramps and reverse. Swift reads the same map through `rc_project_source_map`
  (`ReelProject.sourceMap(_:)`, spec §11 SR-20).

**Why not a wrapping nest.**
- `core/src/format.rs` (250) :27–28, :57–61: `MAX_TRACKS` is 64 and counts every nest's tracks.
  One nest per clip that carries an action costs at least one track each, so a 40-clip edit with
  volume points runs out.
- A nest is a wall elsewhere: `add_blurred_background` refuses a nest clip
  (`core/src/edit_background.rs` (461) :28, :368), `detect_fillers` treats a nest as a wall, and
  bet 1's transcript shows nested words as not editable. A nest clip's own per-pixel properties
  reach no layer (spec §5.3).
- A nest takes a default cross dissolve in place of the clip's own transition (`edit_nest.rs`
  :229–233).
- So this bet makes no nest (VR-6). The framing is composed into the clip's own placement and
  actions instead.

**Backgrounds.** `add_blurred_background` puts its copy on a NEW back-most track
(`edit_background.rs` :12). Called once per clip it would cost one track per clip. VR2 reuses the
copy's builder and puts every backdrop of one run on one track (VR-25).

**Caches and lanes.**
- `app/Sources/MediaCacheLane.swift` (78) :29: the cache lane runs at most two audio decodes
  (peaks, sync, speech) on its own queue, never on the cooperative pool (spec §11 #367).
- `app/Sources/MediaCacheLedger.swift` (231) :37 keys a pass by (cache directory, media id). A
  video pass under the same key would cancel or queue behind the audio passes.
- `MediaImporter.swift` (589) holds the import's `async` and is at the cap. A video pass started
  by a command needs neither.
- The speech cache is computed at import ("never computed at feature time", `silence.md` :21).
  Video analysis costs far more per second, so VR-10 computes it when a command asks.
- These needs are shared with bet 6 (person masks) and bet 5 (mouth activity for one-camera
  shows). They are **CJ1, a shared phase**, specified under "Shared needs" in the risks below and
  in the metadata. VR1 is the first pass to run on CJ1's lane.

**Vision on this SDK (macOS 26.2 SDK; the app's minimum is macOS 26, W-8).**
- `VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest` Revision3 is macOS 12+ (`VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest.h`
  :43; Revision1 is deprecated, :31). It gives a box, a confidence, and roll and yaw.
- `VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` Revision2 is macOS 12+ (`VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest.h`
  :49). It finds full bodies when `upperBodyOnly` is false (:30).
- `VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` Revision2 is macOS 14+
  (`VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest.h` :38). Its `salientObjects` are boxes.
- `VNTrackObjectRequest` (macOS 10.13+) is stateful and is not used (VR-4).
- All four are synchronous `perform` on `VNImageRequestHandler`, as the E9 spike used
  (`tools/proof/effects_spike/vision_common.swift`). The Swift-native requests
  (`DetectFaceRectanglesRequest` and the rest, macOS 15+) answer only through `async perform`
  (`Vision.swiftmodule` interface :346), so they would need a new `async` exception
  (foundations, W-8). They are not used.
- The E9 spike measured `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` and the foreground mask on video.
  Foreground masks flicker frame to frame (`designs/adr/effects-survey.md` :119). Boxes with
  association in the core are the stable signal for framing (VR-4).

**Captions and graphics.**
- Word-style sizes are fractions of `min(W, H)` (`app/Sources/CaptionStyle.swift` (182) :75,
  :146), so the text height is the same on 9:16. Pages are filled to 86 % of the canvas WIDTH by
  the one measuring builder (W-7), so 16:9 pages are about 1.8 times too wide on 9:16 and need
  re-paging. `CaptionLayout.place` (`CaptionLayout.swift`, 581, near the cap) is the one writer of
  `word_style` (W-10) and already replaces caption tracks.
- A graphic's size is frozen at the canvas size when added (G-7). None of the 23 bundled templates
  declares `meta.width`/`height`, so each is added full-canvas. Seventeen use `u =
  Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080`. Six (`lower-third`, `title-card`, `callout`,
  `bar-chart`, `counter`, `kinetic-type`) use `u = ctx.height / 1080`
  (`graphic/tests/graphics/lower-third.js` :20), which grows 1.78 times on a tall canvas.

**The app's edges.**
- Frozen: `EditorViewController.swift`, `PreviewCanvasView.swift` (1121), `AgentServer.swift`,
  `TimelineView.swift`.
- Near or over the cap: `AppDelegate+Menus.swift` (554; `fileMenu()` :119–189),
  `ProjectDocument.swift` (1336; `fileWrapper` :666 carries `cache/`, `media/` and `graphics/`, so
  File ▸ Duplicate's copy keeps the analysis), `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (1454),
  `AgentCatalog+Clips.swift` (574), `core/src/op_table.rs` (374 of a new module's 400; `OP_COUNT`
  :90 is 64; `Kind` :137 is closed), `core/src/scope.rs` (419; `refused_inside` is exhaustive).
- `AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift` (359) :58 has `filledByTheApp`: a tool that does not publish an
  argument its op takes, because the app fills it. That is how `reframe_clip`'s subjects stay out
  of an agent's hands.
- FC's design (bet 4, FC9) needs this bet's step as a function applied to a document it did not
  create (its Make Short documents), with captions left to FC. VR3 provides exactly that (VR-30).

### Decisions to record or amend

Draft text. Each is appended to `designs/spec/11-decisions/creator-jobs.md` in its phase, before
that phase's code, with its row in the index.

**Bet-level, recorded at CJ0.**

- **VR-1 — Auto-reframe is in, as analysis plus ordinary actions.** Subjects are found offline by
  Vision's rectangle and saliency requests on the Mac and cached per media. The core plans the
  framing, and the result is placement and actions on the clip. No mask, no shipped model, and no
  pixel work outside the one-pass compositor. *The sentence for CJ0's §1 rewrite:* "**Auto-reframe
  was on this list until §11 VR-1** (road map 'creator-jobs'): File ▸ Make Vertical Version and
  Clip ▸ Follow Subject find faces, people and salient regions with Vision on the Mac and write
  ordinary actions."
- **VR-2 — Bet 3 needs no key.** Vision's requests are on-device Apple frameworks, outside the key
  rule for language and cloud models. No VR control is disabled for a missing key.
- **VR-3 — A regenerated copy first; linked versions designed and asked at VR7.** The copy needs no
  format change and is the material for the owner's trial. The planner answers a framing path, a
  similarity per instant from the source canvas to the target canvas. The copy composes it into
  each clip. Linked versions would store it per shape. If the owner says no at VR7, VR7–VR9 are
  filed as one issue with this design.
- **VR-4 — Subjects are boxes, detected per sample, never tracked by Vision.**
  `VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest` r3, `VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2 (`upperBodyOnly` false)
  and `VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` r2 run on each sample with a fresh
  `VNImageRequestHandler`. `VNTrackObjectRequest` and every `VNStatefulRequest` are out, so a
  sample's boxes depend on that frame alone, not on where a pass began. Association across samples
  is the core's arithmetic. Masks are out for framing because E9 measured them flickering.
- **VR-5 — The planner is the core's.** Swift measures (decode, Vision) and caches. The core maps
  samples through the clip's speed map, chooses subjects, plans the path, enforces coverage and
  writes actions. The op is a pure function of the project and the samples handed to it, as
  `ripple_delete_ranges` is of Remove Silences' spans.
- **VR-6 — No nest is made to make room for framing.** Framing is composed into the clip's own
  base placement and actions (VR-27). A nest would cost tracks against `MAX_TRACKS` and would wall
  the clip off from blurred backgrounds, filler cuts and the transcript.
- **VR-7 — A followed picture never shows the canvas.** The planner's window always lies inside
  the clip's picture: scale is at least fill and the offsets are clamped by (★). The one exception
  is the "whole" treatment, which is chosen, named in the summary and always paired with a blurred
  backdrop. Every key the planner writes is a covering state, and one curve carries x, y and scale,
  so every frame between keys covers too.

**VR1 — subjects.**

- **VR-10 — Video subjects are computed when a command asks, not at import.** It is the opposite of
  the speech cache's rule, for cost: the speech rule stands for speech. The pass covers only the
  source windows that clips show, plus 1 s each side, and adds to the cache as later commands ask
  for more.
- **VR-11 — The subjects cache.** `cache/subjects/<media id>.bin`, with a marker on §5.6's terms:
  `CacheStamp` plus this kind's constants (the three request revisions, the sample rate, the
  analysis decode size, the compute device and the OS build). It is written last and lists the
  covered sample-index ranges. A stale marker deletes the cache, as for every other kind.
- **VR-12 — The sample grid is source time, `k / rate`.** The rate (first number 5 Hz) and the
  decode's long edge (first number 1280 px) are VR-S1's answer. Every decoded frame in a window
  also gives a 64 × 36 luma signature for VR-14. Images and stills are one sample.
- **VR-13 — Boxes are in the media's displayed frame**: pixels from its top-left, y down, each box
  as its centre, width, height and confidence. Orientation is applied before Vision. The core turns
  boxes into (★)'s Q frame, so a crop never invalidates the cache.
- **VR-14 — Shot changes are measured per frame.** A cut is a frame whose signature's distance from
  the previous frame passes VR-S2's threshold. It is stored as the source time of the new shot's
  first frame. Dissolves are not looked for.
- **VR-15 — HDR and log input.** Read as VR-S1 decides: 8-bit BGRA from the reader, or the
  step-0-converted picture that the thumbnails use for Camera Log, HLG and PQ media.
- **VR-16 — View ▸ Show Subjects is a per-window view state.** It is never persisted, so a proof
  that turns it on moves no defaults key.
- **VR-17 — `get_subjects` answers in clip time** through the app's source map, analysing first when
  the window is not covered. Boxes stay in the media frame.

**VR2 — the planner and Follow Subject.**

- **VR-20 — `reframe_clip {clip, follow, zoom?, where_empty?, replace?, from_width?, from_height?,
  backdrop?, subjects?}`** frames one clip on the current canvas. `from_width`/`from_height` name
  the canvas the clip's placement and actions were authored for, and default to the current one.
  `follow` is `subject` (faces, then people, then salient), `face`, `person`, `salient`, `center`,
  `fit` or `keep`. `keep` is set_canvas's rescale rule composed into the action ends as well.
  `zoom` is 1 to 4 times fill, refused outside. `subjects` is `{size: [w, h], samples: [{t, faces,
  people, salient}], shots: [t]}` in source ticks and VR-13's frame. The op refuses a frame size
  that is not the media's, more than 100,000 samples, more than 8 boxes of a kind in one sample,
  and times that are not strictly increasing, each in its own sentence.
- **VR-21 — Choosing the subject.** Within a shot, boxes are associated by IoU ≥ 0.3 between
  consecutive samples, and a track survives gaps up to 1 s. The primary track has the highest
  presence × median area × centrality. Faces outrank people, and people outrank salient regions; a
  person box containing a tracked face yields to the face. A rival track replaces the primary only
  after it scores 25 % higher for 2 s.
- **VR-22 — Composition.** The subject's face centre sits on the window's vertical centre line. In a
  window taller than wide it sits 38 % of the window's height from the top; otherwise it is
  centred. With no face, the top of the person box sits 12 % from the window's top. These are first
  numbers, set by VR-S3.
- **VR-23 — Moves.** The subject point is median-filtered over 1 s. The window moves only when the
  point leaves a dead zone (±10 % of the window width, ±8 % of its height). A move eases in and out
  for max(0.4 s, distance ÷ 0.5 window widths per second). No move starts within 0.5 s of the last
  one's end unless the subject would leave the window. A still subject makes no move. These are
  first numbers, set by VR-S3.
- **VR-24 — Cuts, loss and two people.**
  - **A shot change is a hard cut in the framing.** It is a one-frame linear action ending exactly
    on the cut's first frame. The new shot's first framing is placed on its subject's median over
    its first second, which the planner can see because it plans a whole clip.
  - **A lost subject is held for 1 s.** After that the planner moves to another track if there is
    one, else eases over 0.8 s to the `where_empty` treatment (`whole` by default, or `center`). It
    comes back once a subject has been seen for 0.6 s.
  - **Two people are framed together when they fit.** When both primary boxes, each widened by
    15 %, fit the window at the chosen zoom, the subject point is their union's. Otherwise the
    planner frames the primary under VR-21's hysteresis.
- **VR-25 — `backdrop`: the blurred copy goes on a named track.** When the framing shows the clip
  whole anywhere, the op adds one blurred copy, built by `add_blurred_background`'s own builder
  (which becomes `pub(crate)`), on the `backdrop` track. When that span is not free there, the copy
  goes on a new back-most track, `paste`'s and `unnest`'s fallback. Without `backdrop`, no copy is
  made. `add_blurred_background` itself is unchanged.
- **VR-26 — What `reframe_clip` refuses.**
  - `follow` other than `keep` on a text, shape, graphic or adjustment clip.
  - A clip with no picture.
  - A nest clip with `subject`, `face`, `person` or `salient`. `center`, `fit` and `keep` are
    allowed.
  - A clip on a matte track, or one a matte cuts, unless `follow` is `keep`.
  - A clip whose base or action rotation is not 0, unless `follow` is `keep`.
  - `subject` with no samples in the clip's window ("clip 12 has no subjects to follow; analyse it
    first").
  - A result equal to the clip is an identity.
- **VR-27 — Compose, or replace.**
  - **Compose, the default.** The framing path F (scale and offset from the source canvas to this
    one) is composed into the clip's base and into the x, y and scale of every action end.
    Framing holds over an existing action are exact, because F is affine in (x, y, scale) and
    commutes with the lerp. The planner schedules its own moves in the gaps between existing
    actions. A move that cannot fit in a gap is carried by the action it overlaps, approximated by
    that action's curve, and still covering by VR-7. A cut inside an existing action splits the
    action there: `set_action` shortens it and `add_action` carries its end and curve, as AU-80's ⌥
    point does.
  - **`replace: true`.** Every x, y and scale key is removed from the clip's action ends first, and
    an action left empty is removed. The base becomes the source canvas's Fit placement, and then F
    is composed. Clip ▸ Follow Subject replaces; Make Vertical Version composes.
- **VR-28 — The tool fills the subjects.** `reframe_clip`'s tool does not publish `subjects`
  (`filledByTheApp`): the handler reads the cache for the clip's window, analysing first. An agent
  that wants a hand-made path writes actions.
- **VR-29 — Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** applies `reframe_clip` with `replace: true` to each selected
  clip that has a picture, as one undo step "Follow Subject". The sheet has Follow (Subject, Faces,
  People, Salient Region, Center), Zoom (100–400 %; the default is 100 % when the canvas's shape
  differs from the picture's and 125 % when it matches, because at 100 % a same-shape picture has
  no room to move) and Where Empty (Show Whole, Center). The sheet remembers Follow and Where Empty
  (`FrameJobFollow*` keys); the tool never reads them (R6-2 read across).

**VR3 — Make Vertical Version.**

- **VR-30 — Make Vertical is one grouped edit applied to a document; the menu applies it to a
  copy.** `VerticalVersion.apply(to:shape:…)` is the step that FC's Make Short calls on its own
  document. File ▸ Make Vertical Version… duplicates through File ▸ Duplicate's path (the package
  with `cache/`, `media/` and `graphics/`) and applies the step there. The source document never
  changes. "Make a copy" is a checkbox, ticked by default and never remembered.
- **VR-31 — The copy opens with the step as its one undo step**, "Make Vertical Version", so Undo in
  the copy shows the 16:9 copy. It is named "<source name> (9:16)" or "(1:1)".
- **VR-32 — Shapes and sizes.** 9:16 and 1:1, keeping the source canvas's short side and even: from
  1920 × 1080 they are 1080 × 1920 and 1080 × 1080. A shape equal to the current canvas is not
  offered. 4:5 is asked at VR3.
- **VR-33 — Which clips are followed.** A top-level media, still or image clip whose rect at its
  first frame spans one whole axis of the canvas (within 1 px) and is centred within 2 % on the
  other is followed with `subject`. A pillarboxed 4:3 or a letterboxed scope picture counts. Every
  other visual top-level clip is `keep`: a camera bubble, a picture-in-picture, a title, a shape,
  a non-full graphic. A full-frame nest clip is `center`. Matte pairs and rotated clips are `keep`
  and are listed.
- **VR-34 — The order of the step.**
  1. `set_canvas {width, height}` with no rescale.
  2. `add_track` at index 0, named "Backgrounds".
  3. `reframe_clip` per visual top-level clip with `from_width`/`from_height` the old canvas and
     `backdrop` that track.
  4. `remove_empty_tracks` limited to that track, when no backdrop was needed.
  5. VR4's captions and graphics.

  Inside a nest nothing changes: a nest is a 16:9 picture.
- **VR-35 — The summary.** The sheet's result lists clips followed, shown whole, kept and not
  followed, each with its reason ("a nest", "rotated", "on a matte track"). `make_vertical_version`
  answers the same lists.
- **VR-36 — `make_vertical_version {shape, follow?, zoom?, where_empty?, captions?, copy?, path?}`**
  mirrors the sheet. It runs off main and never asks. With `copy` (the default) it opens the copy,
  saved at `path` when given, as `new_project` does. With `copy: false` it applies the step to the
  addressed project.
- **VR-37 — Analysis comes before the copy, in the source's cache,** so the copy, a later run and
  the source share it. Cancel during analysis makes nothing.
- **VR-38 — The owner's verdict on vertical versions** (JOB-35), recorded after the trial as GR-9
  was. It says whether the framing, the whole-shot treatment and the captions were what the owner
  would post, and whether re-making copies after master edits was a cost (VR7's question).

**VR4 — captions and graphics.**

- **VR-40 — Word caption pages are re-paged from their own words.**
  - A caption track's pages give their timed words: tokens, `text.words` and the clip's start
    give timeline times. Their style is recognised by face and `word_style` against
    `CaptionStyle`, and their looks by `word_style`'s keys.
  - The words are paged again by the measuring builder through `CaptionLayout.place` with
    `replacing`, on the new canvas, inside the same undo step. W-7 and W-10 stand.
  - A page whose words are untimed, or whose style is not recognised, is kept, placed by `keep`
    and counted.
  - An agent's or FC's run with `captions: false` leaves captions to the caller.
- **VR-41 — Subtitle cues take the Caption preset's measure for the new canvas.**
  - The size is 3.5 % of `min(W, H)`, which equals today's 3.5 % of H on every landscape canvas,
    so a 16:9 project is byte-identical.
  - The wrap is 80 % of W.
  - The box sits 38 % of H below centre on a canvas wider than tall, and 25 % of H (the word
    styles' line) on one taller than wide.
  - A cue that now measures more than two lines is counted in the summary.
- **VR-42 — A graphic the size of the old canvas becomes the size of the new one.** It gets
  `set_graphic {width, height}` with its base x and y 0 and scale 1, and any placement keys in its
  action ends are composed by `keep`. Every other graphic is `keep`.
  - *Amends G-7*, appended: "**Amended <date>, by VR-42:** Make Vertical Version re-sizes a
    graphic whose size is the old canvas to the new canvas, as an explicit `set_graphic`;
    `set_canvas` still never re-lays out a graphic."
- **VR-43 — A bundled template lays itself out inside any canvas.** The six templates that measure
  by `ctx.height / 1080` change to `Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080`. That is the same
  number on every landscape canvas, so their 16:9 renders are byte-identical.
  `docs/graphics-api.md` recommends it.

**VR5 — the cursor (after bet 2's sidecar).**

- **VR-50 — `follow: cursor`.** The subject point is bet 2's recorded cursor, mapped from the
  recording's pixel frame into VR-13's frame. The dead zone is wider (±20 % of the window width).
  A click outside it starts a move that arrives at the click. A typing burst, when bet 2 recorded
  keys, holds the window.
- **VR-51 — A clip with a cursor sidecar is never followed by faces.** On screen content that plays
  a film, a face is not the subject. Make Vertical uses `cursor` for such a clip, and the "whole"
  treatment before VR5 or without a sidecar.
- **VR-52 — Bet 2's 16:9 auto-zooms are replaced in a vertical version** (`replace: true` for
  cursor-followed clips), because the vertical window is already a zoom. Asked at VR5.

**VR6 — the speaker in a two-shot (after bet 5).**

- **VR-60 — `follow: speaker {mics: [clip ids]}`.** Each mic clip's media speech spans, which are
  persisted on the media since AU-110, say who speaks when. A face track is matched to a mic by the
  agreement between its mouth openness and the mic's speech. Mouth openness is the outer-lip height
  ÷ face height from `VNDetectFaceLandmarksRequest` r3, added to VR1's pass as an optional kind.
  The match is the best assignment over at most four.
- **VR-61 — Speaker changes are cuts in the framing**, held at least 2 s. When both speak, the
  framing is the union if it fits, else the last speaker. When agreement is under VR-S1's
  threshold, the sheet asks which face is which mic.

**VR7–VR9 — linked versions (only if the owner says yes at VR7).**

- **VR-70 — A project may hold more than one shape.** The new field is `shapes: [{id, name, width,
  height}]`. The canvas is the main shape. Format N+1 (provisional; 37 today).

    and, since VR-70, other shapes of the same cut."

  meet the clip's own list. A clip with no entry for a shape is placed by `keep`.
  - *Amends §5.4's sentence* "Video, audio and text properties all go through the one list", by
    note: "except a clip's framing for another shape, which is its own list (VR-71)."

### Spikes

Each rule is fixed before its run. Its record goes in the road map.

- **VR-S1 — Vision on video: rate, size, device, determinism, log** (run in CJ0, because it sizes
  CJ1's lane).
  - *Question:* at what sample rate and decode size do the three requests of VR-4 run on decoded
    video fast enough, deterministically enough and accurately enough on the owner's Mac, and does
    log or HDR footage need step 0's conversion first?
  - *Instrument:* `tools/proof/vr_spike/` (synchronous VN* calls, as `effects_spike/vision_job.swift`).
    It decodes with `AVAssetReader`, runs the requests per sample with a compute-device pin,
    times the decode floor and each request, and dumps the boxes. It runs over VR-A, VR-B and
    VR-B2, and over fixtures f1 and f3.
  - *Rules:*
    1. **The rate** is the highest of 10, 5 and 2.5 Hz at which decode plus all three requests run
       at least 3× real time on VR-A at 1080p30 and at least 1.5× at 4K. If none passes: 2.5 Hz,
       with saliency run only on samples with no face or person.
    2. **The decode's long edge** is 1280 px if face recall at 1280 is at least 98 % of recall at
       native size on VR-A and VR-B, else 1920. Recall is the share of sampled frames, in the
       spans the owner marked present, that have a face box overlapping the face.
    3. **The device** is the default if two runs give byte-identical boxes. Otherwise it is the
       CPU when the CPU meets rule 1, else the default, with proofs comparing against the cache
       only (E9's rule).
    4. **Log and HDR:** if face recall on VR-B read as 32BGRA is under 95 % of recall on the same
       clip read through step 0's conversion, VR1 reads converted frames for Camera Log, HLG and PQ
       media (VR-15).
    5. **Human rectangles** are kept if `VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2 finds the person in at
       least 90 % of VR-A's turned-away samples. Otherwise people are dropped from VR-4.
    6. **For VR6:** the agreement threshold is set from VR-C's mouth-openness series against its
       mics.
- **VR-S2 — The shot signature** (with VR1).
  - *Question:* which per-frame signature and threshold find hard cuts inside one flattened clip?
  - *Instrument:* a 32-bin luma histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale per frame, with L1 distance. It
    runs over fixture f4 (known cuts), VR-E's flattened exports (cut lists known from the projects)
    and VR-A (no cuts).
  - *Rule:* the threshold with the highest recall subject to at most one false cut per 10 minutes
    on VR-A. It passes at recall ≥ 98 % on VR-E. If it fails, add 64 × 36 luma SAD as a second
    signal and run again. If that fails, VR-14 ships with the measured recall stated in the guide.
- **VR-S3 — The planner's first numbers** (with VR2, over cached samples, no video).
  - *Question:* which dead zone, pan speed and composition give a talking head that is framed
    without fidget?
  - *Instrument:* the core's planner run from a test binary over VR-A's and VR-E's cached samples.
    The grid is dead zone {6, 10, 15} % × speed {0.3, 0.5, 0.8} windows/s × headroom {33, 38, 42} %.
    It measures containment (the face centre inside the window's central 60 %) and moves per minute.
  - *Rule:* the setting with the highest containment at no more than 6 moves per minute. If no
    setting reaches 97 % containment, the dead zone shrinks one step and the cap rises to 8.
    JOB-31 judges the feel.
- **VR-S4 — A shape switch in the preview** (before VR7's code, only if the owner says yes).
  - *Question:* how long does the preview take to rebuild when the shape changes on a 300-clip
    project, and does a per-shape plan fit the decoder budget?
  - *Rule:* if a rebuild is under 1 s on the owner's Mac, the preview rebuilds on switch. If not,
    it keeps the last two shapes' compositions. A shape whose plan warns past 8 decoders is named
    in the export sheet, as today.

- **Results that move with macOS.** A new OS can change Vision's answers. The marker pins the

- **Timeline clutter.** A long take gets many framing actions on its lane. Each is an ordinary
  action the person can delete.

  tracks need a second. At 64 the step is refused in the core's sentence, nothing is made, and the

  `ctx.width` and `ctx.height` may overflow the tall frame. Only the bundled templates are fixed.
  The guide and `docs/graphics-api.md` say how.
- **Untimed or restyled captions** cannot be re-paged. They are kept, shrunk by `keep`, and counted.
- **Analysis time.** A one-hour recording at 5 Hz takes minutes even windowed. CJ1's sheet has
  Cancel, and the cache makes a second run free.
- **The copy drifts from the master.** That is by design until linked versions exist. JOB-35 says
  whether it matters.
- **Files at the cap.** `op_table.rs` (374 of 400) and `AppDelegate+Menus.swift` (554) take rows and

  VR2 finds it needs a helper there, it pays a pure move first.
- **Linked versions are large.** VR7–VR9 touch every op that carries actions and the
  recipe-and-plan seam. The owner's yes at VR7 is the gate, and VR-S4 runs before the code.

### Not in this bet

- Stacked, side-by-side and corner-bubble layouts, and moving the recorded camera (bet 6). VR uses
  them once they exist.
- Switching between camera angles by speaker (bet 5). VR6 frames one wide shot only.
- Masks, cutouts or any per-pixel subject work. Framing uses boxes alone.
- Following clips inside a nest, matte pairs, or rotated clips. They are kept and listed.
- A language model or cloud model choosing the framing, and Apple FoundationModels.
- Motion blur on pans, stabilisation and optical-flow retiming. These are lifted non-goals, not

- Platform safe-zone overlays and named platform export rows (the next tier's publish slice).
- A range of the timeline as a vertical version. That is FC's New Project from Range or Make Short,
  followed by this step.
- Keyframes. Framing is actions, per §2's idea 3.
